business_scope.primary_industry_name: Remote Desktop Access and Unattended Machine Telemetry Software

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: Civil Law codification with Common Law-informed commercial and financial center practice; no Islamic Sharia application

Canada-Panama Free Trade Agreement (in force 2013; investment chapter)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 23 of 27 April 2015 (Panama AML/CFT framework, as amended), implemented by Executive Decree No. 363 of 2015; Executive Decree No. 92 of 2020 and DGI Resolution No. 201-1659 of 2021 (Final Beneficial Owner Registry administered by the General Directorate of Revenue); Law No. 51 of 2001 (creating the Financial Analysis Unit, UAF); Law No. 25 of 12 June 1995 (Private Interest Foundations, as amended); relevant provisions of the Commercial Code and Notary Law No. 3 of 2006

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney for the formation of the Private Interest Foundation and appointment of the Resident Agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the founder's or beneficial owner's country of origin (e.g., United States state-licensed notary)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority of the country of origin; if the origin country is not a party to the Apostille Convention, full consular legalization at the nearest Panamanian Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing, corporate articles, and incumbency of the founding entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or competent commercial registrar of the founding entity's domicile
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the registry's authenticating ministry or secretary of state; otherwise full consular legalization chain

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Beneficial Ownership Declaration with certified passport copies of all natural persons in the UBO chain
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the beneficial owner's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille over the notarized signature; if non-Hague state, consular legalization at a Panamanian Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference and AML/CFT due diligence letter covering source of funds of the founder and beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank or regulated payment services provider in the founder's country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille of the bank signatory's notarized certificate; alternatively consular legalization where required by the issuing bank's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Spanish translation of the foundation deed and all UBO declarations
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Traductor Publico Autorizado (licensed official translator appointed by the Corte Suprema de Justicia of Panama)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Attestation by the translator's signature and seal; Spanish text requires no apostille, the English/Spanish edition must be annexed

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Apostilled extract of the Public Registry inscription of the Private Interest Foundation (carta constitutiva) after filing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registro Publico de Panama, Direccion General del Registro Publico
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille executed by the Registro Publico de Panama; Ministry of Foreign Affairs certification for certain foreign uses

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of the UBO, founder, resident agent, and any person exercising effective control against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK OFSI consolidated list, and the UAF-Panama list of persons linked to terrorism financing under Law No. 23 of 2015. Beneficial owners identified as PEPs, whether domestic or foreign, must be flagged for enhanced due diligence and senior management approval; any sanctions hit involving embargoed jurisdictions or designated persons triggers immediate refusal and potential suspicious transaction reporting to the UAF.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Publico de Panama online portal - name search and reservation service (Cita Web and Consulta de Firmas; https://www.registropublico.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Private Interest Foundation names must be sufficiently distinct and may be registered in Spanish or any language using Latin script. Non-Spanish names require a certified Spanish translation filed with the inscription; transliteration must avoid graphic or phonetic confusion with existing registered firmas and must not imply a public interest foundation, governmental entity, or regulated financial activity.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: BANK / BANCO (reserved for entities licensed by the Superintendency of Banks)
FINANCIERA / FINANCE COMPANY (requires banking or financial license)
FIDUCIARIA / TRUST (reserved for licensed fiduciary businesses)
SEGUROS / REASEGUROS (reserved for supervised insurers and reinsurers)
FONDO DE INVERSION / MUTUAL FUND (requires collective investment scheme authorization)
BOLSA DE VALORES / STOCK EXCHANGE (reserved for securities exchange licensees)
COOPERATIVA / COOPERATIVE (subject to cooperative legislation and prior authority)
REPUBLICA DE PANAMA / GOBIERNO NACIONAL / PRESIDENCIA / MINISTERIO (official state identity misrepresentation)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant through the licensed resident agent files a written reconsideration and appeal with the Direccion General del Registro Publico within five (5) business days of notification. The Registrar must decide within thirty (30) days. An adverse final decision may be appealed administratively within the same registry and ultimately through an action before the Sala Tercera de la Corte Suprema de Justicia. A name rejected for confusing similarity may be resubmitted in corrected form immediately; reservation extension beyond the initial 30 calendar days requires a new filing and payment of the prevailing registry tariff.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted in ordinary practice only to the extent the statutory seat and registered address are maintained at the licensed resident agent's premises in Panama. A virtual or remote commercial address used for teleworking, sales, or support functions is acceptable for a remote desktop software and IoT telemetry business, but the foundation must keep all corporate records, UBO data, and minute books at the resident agent's office and make them available to the DGI, UAF, and competent courts.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate quantified risk: approximately 10-15% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection or documentary audit in any calendar year for a low-risk software services entity, with higher scrutiny only if sanctions or PEP flags arise.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and statutory address maintenance at the resident agent's premises - first annual period
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark; frequently bundled with resident agency fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/KYC, PEP, and sanctions screening package (UBO piercing; OFAC, UN, EU, and UAF blacklist checks)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed compliance fee per beneficial owner; prevailing market range USD 200-400

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Public Registry inscription stamps and transcription fees for the foundation deed

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Panama Private Interest Foundation Law), Articles 1, 5, 8, 15, 20, 25 and 28; subsidiary application of Ley 32 de 1927 and the Panamanian Civil Code.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Panama Public Registry), Juridical Persons Section (Sección de Personas Jurídicas)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública No. ______ – Charter of Constitution of a Private Interest Foundation (Acta Constitutiva de Fundación de Interés Privado)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Statutory adequate-capital test under Law 25, Article 20; registry tariff scale requires a minimum stated foundation capital of B/.10,000.00 (Ten Thousand Balboas) to attract the standard B/.300.00 one-time capital tax. The capital constitutes the foundation patrimony and is not subject to a paid-up escrow account requirement at formation; asset contributions may be delivered by the Founder by way of a separate contribution statement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION — The Foundation Council, meeting at the registered office on [DATE], unanimously resolved: (1) The initial capital of Ten Thousand Balboas (B/.10,000.00) declared in the Foundation Charter is subscribed as the permanent endowment, and the capital tax has been settled with the Public Registry. (2) The registered office at [ADDRESS], Panama City, Republic of Panama, is adopted as the legal seat and operational domicile. (3) [NAME] is appointed Founder, [NAMES] Council Members, and [NAME] Protector, with charter powers. (4) The Council is authorized to open bank accounts, execute digital commerce agreements, and engage payment processors (Stripe, Paddle) for the software business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Name Clearance Desk (through an accredited Panamanian notary or attorney)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the Panamanian counsel to submit the proposed foundation name to the Public Registry name-search system. The name must include the suffix Fundación or Foundation and must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered entity. Obtain the non-registration certificate as a condition precedent to drafting the charter.
required_dossiers: Proposed foundation name plus two alternative names
Certified copy of legalized identification of the Founder
Name search request form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is unavailable or objected to, file a brief with the Public Registry requesting reservation of an alternative name or append a distinguishing prefix or descriptor; re-instruct the notary once clearance is granted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial Execution of the Foundation Charter (Escritura Pública)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the Republic of Panama (licensed by the Corte Suprema de Justicia)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Foundation Charter in Spanish, appointing the Founder, Foundation Council, optional Protector, and first beneficiaries; declare foundation capital of B/.10,000.00; designate the resident agent; fix the registered office; execute the deed before the Notary, who protocolizes and issues the Escritura Pública. Pay notarial fees according to the official notary tariff.
required_dossiers: Foundation Charter draft
Name clearance certificate
Certified passports of Founder and Council Members
Proof of residential address of the Founder (know-your-customer file)
Reserved statement of beneficiaries
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any defect in the executed deed is corrected by a notarial amendment instrument (adenda) executed before the same notary prior to submission to the Public Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Foundation Charter and Payment of Capital Tax
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Juridical Persons Section (Sección de Personas Jurídicas)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the notarized Escritura Pública for inscription through the Registry reception and distribution office or via the e-filing platform. Pay the one-time foundation capital tax of B/.300.00 (equivalent to 1% of the B/.10,000.00 declared capital) at the National Bank of Panama or through the registry e-payment gateway. The registration is constitutive and takes effect from the presentation number date.
required_dossiers: Notarized Escritura Pública (original and one copy)
Official receipt of payment of the foundation capital tax
Registry cover sheet or filing application
Notarized power of attorney of the legal representative (if filing electronically)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a notice of defect or query, counsel files a rectification brief within 30 business days, submits the corrected instrument, or executes a supplementary notarial deed; if the time limit lapses, the deed is re-presented with new filing fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Foundation Certificate and Tax Identification (RUC) Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (certificate issuance) and Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Ministry of Economy and Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Request the certified copy of inscription (Certificación de Inscripción) of the Foundation from the Registry. Thereafter register with DGI to obtain the RUC (tax identification number) for the foundation, record its territorial-tax status, and register as an employer at the CSS (Caja de Seguro Social) if personnel will be engaged.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the inscribed Foundation Charter
RUC application form (Solicitud de Registro Único de Contribuyente)
Identification and appointment certificate of the legal representative
Proof of registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI requests further information, submit a sworn declaration on the territorial source of income and, where applicable, a non-activity letter for foreign-sourced funds; any RUC data errors are cured by an amendment application at the DGI attended desk.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the Aviso de Operación and Issuance of the Municipal Commercial Patent
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipalidad de Panamá – Dirección de Atención al Contribuyente (municipal online portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Aviso de Operación on the municipal portal, classifying the activity under ISIC 6201 / NAICS 511210 (remote desktop access and telemetry software), pay the municipal patent fee calculated on declared capital, and obtain the patent certificate. This license authorizes commercial invoicing, office operations, and hiring in the District of Panama.
required_dossiers: RUC certificate
Certified copy of the institution inscription of the Foundation
Identification of the legal representative
Rental agreement or title deed for the registered office
Completed Aviso de Operación form with estimated personnel count
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Municipal corrections, such as an incorrect activity code, are resolved by filing a revised aviso on the portal within five working days; patent fee recalculations may be challenged by a reconsideration petition to the Municipal Treasury.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipalidad de Panamá – Department of Commercial Patents and Municipal Engineering Directorate
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Patente Municipal Comercial / Aviso de Operación (Municipal Commercial Patent and Operation Notice)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente de Panamá (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Evaluación Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I – Environmental Registration. The activity is purely software distribution, remote desktop access, and telemetry data processing, which generates no industrial effluents or hazardous emissions. A full Environmental Impact Study (Category III) is not triggered; only a brief e-registration notice to MiAMBIENTE is required for the registered office.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater, VOC, or particulate emission thresholds apply to pure software licensing. If optional IoT gateway or demotelemetry hardware staging is hosted, the operation must observe de-minimis compliance with Executive Decree No. 23 of 1966 (air emissions), Decree No. 8 of 8 May 2009 (aquatic discharge permits), and Basel Convention e-waste handling rules; solid waste must be collected by authorized municipal operators.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety Visto Bueno (Certificate of Fire Inspection) from the Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de la República de Panamá; structural load verification for any server, rack, or telemetry equipment rooms by the municipal engineering office; occupational health and safety registration with MITRADEL (Occupational Health and Safety Directorate); and emergency evacuation plan approval by SINAPROC for any office exceeding ten employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas – tax portal: 'e-Tax Panama' (https://etax.dgi.gob.pa; public information portal: https://www.dgi.gob.pa)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-held Private Interest Foundation (PIF), the statutory tax identifier is the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente), which serves simultaneously as the income-tax and ITBMS (VAT) registration number. The foundation must first appoint a resident agent and be registered in the Registro Público of Panama. Thereafter, the foundation president or legal representative files Form RUC-L (persona jurídica) with the DGI through e-Tax or a Regional Office, attaching the foundation charter, public registration certificate, resident agent's notarized acceptance, and identity documents of the council members. A nominal processing fee (subject to DGI current tariff) is paid. Upon issuance, the DGI provides an 'Aviso de Inscripción' and activates VAT obligations if the foundation undertakes taxable commercial transactions in Panama. A foreign entity merely establishing or sponsoring a PIF does not itself require a Panamanian RUC; the foundation is the taxpayer.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not operate a check-the-box entity classification system. A PIF is automatically a separate juridical person under Law 25 of 1995 and is taxable on Panama-source income only. No hybrid mismatch elections are available. The PIF may elect to satisfy its Panamanian tax presence through the flat annual foundation tax when it confines its activities to passive wealth management or foreign-source operations; if it carries on a commercial or industrial activity in Panama, it becomes a fully registered territorial taxpayer and must report Panama-source income under the general rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto de Transferencias de Bienes Muebles y Prestación de Servicios (ITBMS / VAT)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary de minimis threshold applies: any person or entity conducting taxable transfers of movable goods or taxable services within Panama must register for ITBMS. A simplified small-taxpayer regime is available only for domestic taxpayers with annual gross turnover not exceeding PAB 36,000; this does not exempt a foreign PIF from registration when it exports zero-rated services or makes taxable local supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama mandates electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica) for all ITBMS-registered enterprises. Invoices must be issued in XML format, digitally signed using a certificate issued by a DGI-accredited certification authority, and transmitted in real time to DGI's e-Tax platform through web services/API for validation and clearance. Validated invoices are returned with a DGI verification code and QR code that must be printed or embedded on the customer copy. Zero-rated export invoices require prior electronic transmission of the export declaration (Computo de Exportación) to DGI; paper invoices are not accepted for export zero-rating.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available for the physical export of tangible goods from Panama and for offshore services, including remote desktop access, unattended-machine telemetry, screen-sharing software subscriptions, and IoT remote support services, provided the service is supplied to a non-Panamanian customer, is effectively performed outside Panama, or the benefit/effective use occurs entirely abroad. The taxpayer must demonstrate from the contract, server location, user logs, and payment routing that the recipient is non-resident and that no use or entertainment of the service takes place in Panama. Services rendered to a Panamanian resident or effectively used in Panama will be subject to ITBMS at 7% irrespective of the digital delivery mechanism.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única de Aduanas de Exportación)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / Alternative transport document for digital services evidencing delivery architecture
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT/MT103 message showing payment received from the non-resident customer
Export service contract incorporating scope of remote screen share and IoT telemetry services
Commercial invoice annotated 'ZERO-RATED EXPORT – OFFSHORE SERVICE'
Certificate of non-residence or corporate registry/tax ID extract of the foreign customer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI may audit zero-rated export claims for five years after filing. If the exporter cannot produce the customs, contractual, technical, and banking evidence proving foreign destination, offshore effective use, or receipt of foreign currency, the zero-rating is retroactively revoked. Reinstated ITBMS at 7% becomes exigible with monthly late-payment surcharges and adjusted interest. Administrative fines may range from a minimum monetary penalty to 100% of the evaded tax, and input VAT credits previously refunded may be clawed back with penalty. Wilful use of false export declarations or fabricated service contracts in a digital services context constitutes tax fraud, which may lead to criminal prosecution before Panamanian courts and suspension or cancellation of the taxpayer's electronic invoicing authorization.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama operates a fully dollarized economy with no central bank empowered to issue currency or impose exchange controls. Banking supervision and financial regulation are exercised by the Superintendency of Banks of Panama (Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá, SBP) under Decree Law No. 2 of 22 February 2008, while the Financial Analysis Unit (Unidad de Análisis Financiero, UAF) administers AML/CFT oversight. The Balboa (PAB) is a legal-tender unit of account at statutory 1:1 parity with the US Dollar, which circulates as the sole paper currency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility exists on both current and capital account. Panama imposes no exchange controls, no central bank approval for inward or outward remittances, and no restriction on profit or capital repatriation. A Private Interest Foundation (PIF) engaged in cross-border software exports may freely denominate contracts, hold multi-currency accounts, and remit founder or council distributions, subject only to the territorial source-based income tax regime of the Tax Code, DGI Resolution 201-9306 of 2019 on the digital economy, and standard DGI statistical/declaration obligations. Profit remittances are not taxed at source when the underlying income is derived exclusively from outside Panamanian territory, but outbound payments for services rendered into Panama may attract the 12.5% non-resident withholding tax.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Panama imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no obligation to repatriate or sell foreign currency receipts to the state or banking system. Export proceeds from remote software and IoT telemetry services may be retained in USD or any convertible currency in domestic or foreign banks without reporting to a central bank.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility with structural constraints. Panama does not maintain a general-purpose Electronic Money Institution (EMI) licensing track for non-bank firms; the SBP operates an innovation hub and is developing a fintech licensing framework, but a PIF cannot act as its own PSP. Offshore digital EMIs generally decline PIF structures without strong economic-substance narratives and complete KYC bundles; the practical route is a local commercial bank account fed by PSP settlement from Stripe and Paddle via SWIFT, with direct EMI usage limited to treasury-float diversification below 15% of monthly receipts or emergency redundancy.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is permitted under SBP CDD rules when supported by continuous authenticated video-conference verification, electronic or notarized signatures, and the PIF's registered agent certifying the Foundation Charter. In practice, most tier-1 banks require at least one live video interview with the founder or a Foundation Council member and full beneficial-ownership identification; physical appearance of directors is generally waived, although the bank may request a board resolution recorded in the Public Registry and a notarized corporate certificate. Final approval remains at bank compliance discretion.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PIF with no commercial substance and no evidentiary link to software operations
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Foundation Charter (Acta de Fundación) and Bylaws stating the remote-software purpose; certified copy of the Public Registry filing; Foundation Council appointment minutes; virtual-office lease or registered-agent service agreement; Aviso de Operación and RUC certificate; audited profit-and-loss statement reconciling Stripe/Paddle settlements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Red-flag dual-use software profile: remote desktop access and unattended telemetry presenting fraud, BEC, or malware risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Technical whitepaper and customer success files; B2B end-user vetting and acceptable-use policy; SOC 2 Type II report, ISO/IEC 27001 certificate, and DPIA; comprehensive terms of service prohibiting misuse; self-assessment confirming de-minimis export classification under Wassenaar/CAT 5D2.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity in ultimate beneficial ownership due to Foundation Council and protector powers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: UAF Transparency Registry filing identifying every beneficial owner; passport copies, residential proof, and professional references for each owner; registered-agent compliance-contact waiver; formal beneficial-ownership chart with explanations of council vs. protector powers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border settlement mismatch: credits arriving from PSP omnibus accounts and wallet providers rather than named end clients
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Verified Stripe and Paddle dashboard excerpts naming the PIF as merchant/beneficiary; signed PSP Merchant Agreements; consolidated invoicing ledger with payout reference ID mapping; daily SWIFT reconciliation and purpose-code narrative for each incoming credit.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Founder or shareholder capital wiring is executed via SWIFT MT103 to the PIF operational account, referencing 'Capital Contribution / PIF Funding'; Panama imposes no FX approval or purpose-code mandate, but the beneficiary field must include the 20-digit Código de Cuenta Cliente (CCC) and the PIF RUC to ensure straight-through processing. Single injections above USD 10,000 trigger UAF transaction-reporting thresholds under Law 23 of 2015, so a pre-assembled evidentiary bundle of the capital call, founder resolution, Council minute, source-of-funds statements, and independent counsel validation must be maintained at the bank and with the resident agent for DGI territorial filing.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 for supplier invoices, SaaS royalty payments, and operating expenses, with MT202 covers used for internal liquidity sweeps. For software licensing and infrastructure procurement above USD 50,000, a commercial letter of credit may be opened, although PSP-based vendor remittances (Paddle payouts) render bank-issued LCs unnecessary in most cases. Each disbursement must carry a documented delegation of authority, beneficiary KYC, invoice-match, underlying contract, and FX conversion memo for non-USD payables; DGI records require payment vouchers and, where Panamanian withholding applies, tax-residency evidence for the counterparty.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Natural-hedge policy: multi-currency settlement accounts (EUR, GBP, BRL, COP) with tier-1 banks to match PSP payout currencies and avoid derivatives for sub-USD 250,000 quarterly exposure.
Deliverable FX forwards: permitted on cumulative non-USD exposure above USD 250,000 equivalent per quarter through SBP-licensed banks, with an aggregate notional cap of 20% of gross annual receipts.

Cross-currency swaps: permissible for EUR/GBP-denominated PSP float held for 90 days or longer, executed under ISDA or a bank Master Agreement and confirmed by the Foundation Council treasury resolution.

Non-deliverable forwards: permitted only for settlement against COP, BRL, or ARS through an offshore bank when local counterparty liquidity is absent; notional capped at USD 100,000 per trade and subject to monthly valuation monitoring.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Government Tax on Private Interest Foundation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 15 January for the preceding calendar year; grace period until 15 March with applicable surcharge
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment incurs a 10% surcharge within the first 30 days and an additional US$50 after 30 days; non-payment for two consecutive years may result in administrative strike-off and dissolution by the Registro Público de Panamá.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days of any change in the Foundation Council, protector, founder, or beneficiaries; no zero-change annual filing required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance with UBO record-keeping and update duties may result in fines ranging from USD 500 to USD 10,000 pursuant to Law 70 of 2019, as amended.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Good Standing Confirmation Through Registered Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (acting through the licensed resident agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous; the resident agent must confirm timely payment of the annual tax and maintain the registered office and agent status throughout the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain a resident agent or registered office can lead to administrative dissolution and loss of legal personality; the foundation may also be struck off for non-payment of the annual tax for two consecutive years.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is imposed on Panama Private Interest Foundations (PIF) under Law 25 of 1995, regardless of asset value, revenue, or number of beneficiaries. A mandatory audit may arise only where the Foundation Charter expressly designates an auditor, or where the DGI requires audited financial statements because the foundation engages in taxable commercial activity in Panama above the applicable gross receipts threshold; in standard passive holding structures no independent audit is required.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in Panama / IFRS for SMEs if voluntary financial statements are prepared; no statutory filing of financial statements is required for a PIF with the Public Registry or tax authorities unless it produces Panama-source income for which tax disclosure is needed.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: PIFs have no share capital or registered shareholders; beneficial ownership is expressed through the founder, Foundation Council, protector, and named or discretionary beneficiaries. There is no annual zero-change UBO confirmation. Any change in beneficial ownership must be recorded and transmitted through the licensed resident agent to the DGI UBO Registry within 30 calendar days. The resident agent must maintain the UBO records and a customer due diligence file current throughout the year.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Foundation Charter and all notarial amendments
Register of Foundation Council Members and Protector
Minute Book of Foundation Council Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 – 850 per annum for a Panamanian resident agent, registered office and compliance correspondence
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,200 – 4,500 per annum for an optional voluntary stewardship audit prepared for banks, investors, or licensing counterparties; no mandatory audit fee applies

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 0% effective rate on foreign-source receipts under Panama's territorial tax system; no general tax holiday applies to ISIC 6201 remote software services. The only meaningful preferential feature for a Private Interest Foundation engaged in cross-border remote screen-share/IOT telemetry is the non-inclusion of non-Panama source income. Profits distributed from foreign-source earnings are not subject to Panamanian dividend withholding, producing a fully exempt exit route. Panama-source income from within the territory remains taxable at the 25% corporate rate with no special software-export credit.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 510 – Declaración Jurada Anual del Impuesto sobre la Renta (Annual Corporate Income Tax Return); filed via the DGI e-tax portal (Sistema Panamá en Línea / DGI Virtual) using the RUC and registered digital signature.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the close of the fiscal year; for calendar-year taxpayers the return is due on or before 31 March of the following taxable year. Non-calendar electing entities must file no later than 31 May of the year in which the statutory three-month window matures.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 – RUC / Registro Único de Contribuyente
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unique taxpayer identification number of the Private Interest Foundation, as issued by the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PIF must obtain a Panamanian RUC even when all shareholders/beneficiaries are non-residents; foreign beneficial owner information is collected through the RUC registration record.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Indicates the initial and closing dates of the reporting taxable year (DD/MM/YYYY to DD/MM/YYYY).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities are bound to the calendar year unless an express DGI-approved different fiscal period is registered.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 – Actividad Económica Principal (Main Economic Activity)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIIU / ISIC classification code of the primary commercial activity, for remote desktop access software and telemetry services this is ISIC 6201.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident-owned PIF must declare 'provisión de software de acceso remoto y telemetría IoT desde territorio panameño' or, where applicable, 'servicios de soporte remoto sin PE en Panamá' with the same ISIC scope.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 – Ingresos Gravables de Fuente Panameña (Taxable Panama-Source Income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenues derived from customers located in Panama, services performed within Panamanian territory, or use of intangible rights in Panama. Such income is subject to the 25% corporate rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign sales of remote screen-share subscriptions and IOT telemetry to non-Panamanian customers should be excluded entirely from this line. Where a mixed global revenue pool exists, the taxpayer must maintain geolocation, server-route, contract-execution, and customer-billing evidence to sustain the exclusion.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 – Ingresos Exentos / Fuente Extranjera (Exempt or Foreign-Source Income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Receipts earned outside Panama or from international markets, including SaaS revenue from non-resident subscribers, foreign-server telemetry data processing, and offshore remote-management fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PIFs rely on this line to reduce effective Panamanian tax to near zero. The exemption is defeated if the commercial activity is deemed to occur inside Panama, e.g., Panamanian-domiciled servers, local data-centre connectivity, or support services physically rendered in Panama.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 – Costos y Deducciones Relacionados (Related Costs and Deductions)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowed operating expenses attributable to Panama-source income, including payroll, cloud infrastructure, depreciation of telemetry hardware, and third-party licensing costs incurred in Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only costs directly related to taxable Panama-source revenue are deductible. Foreign-source expenditures should not be allocated against Panama-source income unless a supported and consistent apportionment method is disclosed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 – Renta Neta Imponible (Net Taxable Income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Resulting figure after subtracting Panama-source costs and deductions from Panama-source gross revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the PIF is passive and earns no Panama-source revenue, this field should be zero or negative; negative balances are carried forward up to five taxable years.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 – Impuesto Determinado (Corporate Income Tax at 25%)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The final assessed tax computed as 25% of the net taxable income (Box 7), before prepayments and withholding credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where the statutory tax of 25% produces a positive figure, the PIF must pay it even if all ultimate shareholders are foreign residences; treaty relief does not apply to corporate-level income tax in Panama.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 9 – Pagos a Cuenta, Retenciones y Anticipos (Prepayments, Withholdings, and Advance Tax Credits)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for quarterly/mensual prepayments, any advanced dividend tax, credits for taxes withheld by Panamanian customers, and other instalments paid to the DGI.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PIFs will typically show zero prepayments unless they hold a Panamanian revenue-generating asset or a Panamanian customer withholding mechanism applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 10 – Cuota a Pagar o Saldo a Favor (Tax Due or Carryback Credit)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final balance due to the DGI or the excess prepayment credit to be offset against future obligations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: After offsets, any remaining balance must be paid on or before the filing deadline. A negative balance is not refunded automatically; it can be carried forward as a credit in the following taxable year.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty accrues at 2% of the tax due for each month or fraction of month, capped at 10%; failure to file within an additional six months may result in the DGI issuing administrative assessment, a fine of USD 500 to USD 5,000, suspension of the RUC, and criminal liability if fraudulent intent is established. Persistent non-filing of Form 510 exposes the PIF's appointed resident agent and directors to personal enforcement actions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 605 – Información de Operaciones con Partes Relacionadas (Annual Transfer Pricing Information Return); filed electronically through the DGI e-tax portal by all taxpayers engaged in related-party transactions above the statutory threshold.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due no later than six months after the fiscal year-end; for calendar-year taxpayers the statutory filing window closes on 30 June of the following year. Local File/Master File documentation must be prepared and submitted to DGI only upon specific administrative request, but it must exist as of the filing date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: RUC and denominación of the Private Interest Foundation filing the transfer-pricing return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident owner does not replace the Panamanian PIF as the filing taxpayer; the return is submitted in the name of the PIF with its Panama RUC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 – Relación de Operaciones con Vinculadas (Related-Party Transaction Schedule)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate description of transactions with related entities, including remote software licensing fees paid to or received from foreign group companies, cloud infrastructure purchases from affiliates, and management or technical service charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PIFs must report even the foreign-source transactions with related parties if they are reflected in the foundation's books; Panama applies a symmetric TP documentation regime to foreign-source related-party transactions where they affect the Panamanian entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 – Método de Precio de Transferencia Aplicado (Transfer Pricing Method Applied)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Indicates the selected OECD-aligned arm's length method, including CUP, resale price, cost-plus, transactional net margin method (TNMM), or profit split.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For remote software services and IOT telemetry intragroup fees, the TNMM is the most common; a properly documented net margin benchmark study is expected for every related-party transaction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name, tax residence, and relationship of each related party involved in the cross-border transaction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident parent company must be identified by its foreign tax identification number and jurisdiction; failure to disclose the ultimate beneficial owner raises red flags under both TP and AML rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 – Monto Total y Tipo de Transacción (Transaction Amount and Type)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross amount in USD, type of transaction (goods, services, royalties, interest, financing), and the geographic source of the income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Separate identification of Panama-source and foreign-source related-party flows is required; amounts attributable to pure foreign-source technical services should be clearly flagged as territorial-exempt to avoid erroneous taxation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file Form 605 carries a fine of USD 1,000 to USD 10,000; inaccurate or incomplete filings attract an additional USD 5,000 penalty. Where the DGI later determines that a transfer-pricing adjustment is warranted, the taxpayer is liable for the tax deficiency plus a late-payment surcharge of 1% per month, and may be subject to a corrective penalty of 40% of the omitted tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory withholding on dividends distributed from Panama-source profits; reduced to 5% where the underlying profits have already borne the full 25% corporate income tax; dividend distributions originating exclusively from foreign-source profits under the territorial regime are exempt from Panamanian withholding tax. For a Private Interest Foundation distributing cross-border software revenue to non-resident beneficiaries, the practical WHT exposure is 0% provided the income was foreign-source and no Panama corporate tax accrued.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama has a limited bilateral double-tax network; the applicable DTT (e.g., France, Portugal, Singapore, Spain, Mexico) may reduce dividend WHT where the recipient is a company or foundation resident of that treaty state. The protocol requires: (1) issuance of a written request for treaty benefit by the non-resident recipient; (2) submission of a valid Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) covering the payment year, sealed and apostilled or legalised, with an official Spanish translation where required; (3) completion of the DGI form for reduced withholding application through the e-tax portal; and (4) retention of the authoritative documentary trail in Panama for at least six years. If the TRC is not presented before remittance, the statutory rate must be applied and a subsequent refund claim may be pursued. Panama will not grant treaty relief to a beneficiary that lacks economic substance or is merely a conduit shell.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Panama-source royalties paid to non-residents, including license fees for the use of software, patents, or telemetry technology inside Panama, are subject to a 12.5% gross withholding tax as the final non-resident income tax; DTT rates may reduce or zero this tax under applicable protocols. Interest paid to non-resident unaffiliated commercial lenders on foreign debt used to fund the global remote software business is generally exempt from Panamanian withholding; however, interest paid to related foreign intermediaries or shareholders is subject to scrutiny under thin-capitalisation principles and can be recharacterised as a taxable dividend or royalty, attracting the 12.5% royalty/12.5% non-resident service withholding rate as appropriate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Law 70 of 2019 and its Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) impose a substance-based standard on Panamanian tax-resident entities, including Private Interest Foundations, that carry on relevant activities such as distribution, service provision, financing, headquarters, shipping, holding, and intellectual-property holding. Remote screen-share software development, IOT telemetry processing, and related technical support will fall within the 'provision of services' relevant activity. The PIF must therefore demonstrate in Panama: (i) the active management and direction of the business; (ii) a physical office or data-centre presence commensurate with the level of activity; (iii) adequate number of full-time employees physically present in Panama; and (iv) operational expenditure in Panama proportionate to the foreign revenue booked. A pure passive holding PIF that owns IP rights without local staff or decision-making will be deemed to lack economic substance, triggering a regulatory review and possible denial of the territorial exemption or treaty access. The Panama ESR requires annual reporting to the Superintendencia de Sujetos No Financieros, and non-compliance is subject to fines of USD 5,000 for incorrect filings and up to USD 100,000 for intentional failure to meet substance thresholds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate under-declaration of Panama-source income, such as routing remote screen-share and telemetry services to Panamanian corporate customers through a foreign shell without reporting the Panamanian economic nexus, or falsely classifying Panama-source SaaS revenue as foreign-source.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty of 50% of the omitted tax plus accrued monthly surcharges (1% per month); sham structures are disregarded and the full 25% corporate income tax is reassessed. Criminal prosecution may result in imprisonment of 1 to 5 years and a fine of two to ten times the amount evaded, depending on the gravity of fraudulent intent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the resident agent of the PIF may have the corporate veil pierced if they knowingly participated in the evasion scheme; the court can impose joint civil liability for the tax debt, travel bans, disqualification from acting as directors of Panamanian entities, and custodial sentences for ancillary offences under the Criminal Code.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an active ISIC 6201 remote software and IoT telemetry business through a PIF that has no employees, office, server assets, or board decisions in Panama, while simultaneously claiming the territorial tax exemption and treaty benefits for the foreign-derived income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The DGI and ESR authorities may deny the tax exemption, reclassify the income as Panama-source if telemetry equipment or management decision-making is deemed located in Panama, and impose administrative fines of USD 5,000 to USD 100,000. Repeat violations cause cancellation of the foundation's registration with the Registro Público.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Beneficial owners and directors who sign statutory declarations of substance that are false are subject to criminal perjury-like sanctions; they may be ordered to pay the unpaid corporate taxes out of their personal estates, have their international travel barred, and be debarred from holding office in Panama for up to ten years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing intra-group licensing or intragroup telemetry processing services below arm's length, thereby stripping value from the Panamanian foundation or shifting Panama-source profits to a zero-tax foreign affiliate without economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The DGI may reassess taxable income under the arm's length principle, apply a 40% corrective penalty on the under-assessed tax, levy interest at the official rate plus a 10% per annum surcharge, and reject the PIF's requested treaty relief for the correlated foreign income. Repeat conduct qualifies as tax fraud for criminal referral.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who failed to establish and document a robust TP policy are jointly and severally liable for the additional tax assessed; the court can freeze personal assets, impose director disqualification, and in egregious cases order the imprisonment of the decision-makers who approved the non-arm's length contracts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Private Interest Foundation to hide the identity of the true owner of the remote software company or to receive telemetry subscription revenue without filing a beneficial ownership declaration with the Panamanian registry, or ignoring the ESR notification requirement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Failure to maintain and file accurate beneficial ownership information attracts monetary penalties of USD 1,000 to USD 1,000,000 under Law 23 of 2015 and its implementing decrees. Criminal laundering of subscription and remittance proceeds can independently warrant imprisonment of 5 to 12 years and forfeiture of all assets connected to the offence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The nominee directors and the registered agent face immediate personal criminal liability for knowingly allowing an undisclosed beneficial owner, including debarment, travel bans, extradition treaties activated, and incarceration. The civil veil of the PIF is automatically lifted so that the concealed owner becomes personally accountable for unpaid tax and money-laundering fines.
